To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

we have designed a modular protein origami fold that can be assembled into a triangular bipyramid from two chains, and that we have devised a strategy for a conformational switch in this two chain complex.
we have designed and characterised a de novo triangular CC based bipyramidal protein cage and devised a two chain self assembly strategy for its formation.
we have devised a modular strategy for two chain self assembly and proteolysis induced regulation of CCPO folds.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the design and construction of CCPO nanostructures and the development of strategies to regulate the conformational state of the nanostructure.
the design of CCPO nanostructures, their self assembly from two chains, and regulation of the resulting assemblies by proteolysis.
the design and regulation of protein nanoarchitectures from modular building blocks.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

we have developed a modular design strategy to generate two-chain CC-based nanostructures, and that we have shown that the CC-based nanostructures can be used for the generation of dynamic nanostructures.
the CCPO approach is a powerful tool in the design of modular protein assemblies and the introduction or regulation of functions.
the design of CCPOs is a modular approach for the de novo construction of polypeptide cages and that this strategy can be used to engineer multi-chain complexes.

The main takeaway from our work is that
the CCPO strategy can be used to design and program the self assembly of complex multi chain polypeptide nanoassemblies.
the design of CCPOs can be extended to more complex assemblies by using the self assembly of pre organised structural units.
CCPO could be used for the design of dynamic and programmable protein nanostructures, which could facilitate the construction of complex assemblies with a broad range of functionalities.
